description.p: Hermitage is a single-user, local-first media sanctuary for your Calibre library. It opens your existing Calibre database read-only and renders the library as an edge-to-edge cover-art grid with a sliding detail pane, a tag-tree genre browser, a series browser, and an at-a-glance Library Insights window.

ul.li: Cover-art grid with per-cover dynamic colour glow
Codex detail view with hero-blur header, ISBN/Goodreads/etc. links
Genre browser using Calibre's dot-separated tag hierarchy
Calibre-compatible search query language with virtual library support
Local reading history (recent shelf, read indicator, last-opened line)
Library Insights — top tags/authors, format coverage, hygiene audit
Bundled premium typography (Fraunces, Inter, IBM Plex Sans Condensed)
100% local — zero telemetry, zero accounts, zero network calls

description.p: 1.0 Milestone and Stable Release. All core end-to-end features — the first-run wizard, search syntax, virtual library sidebars, dynamic covers, reading history, and OS document hooks — are verified stable under Wayland and Hyprland.

Preferences, Library Insights, Keyboard Shortcuts, and About now report the application's own window identity to the compositor instead of falling back to the interpreter's name, so a window rule written for Hermitage matches these windows too. Also quiets a warning printed on every launch.

Calibre custom columns land in the Codex. User-defined columns (reading status, source, translators, date read, and any others) now show in a new Details section, read-only, and are searchable with Calibre's #label: syntax. Text and enumeration values render as clickable pills that filter the library on an exact match; dates, numbers, and booleans render as plain lines.

Hyprland-native redesign: libadwaita is dropped in favour of plain GTK 4 and a stylesheet Hermitage owns outright, themed Kanagawa Dragon and still following the system light/dark preference through the desktop portal. The Codex and virtual-library sidebars now float over the grid, the window wears no title buttons (Ctrl+Q quits), a quarter-tile drops to a clean single column, and a new keyboard shortcuts window, grid type-ahead find, and HiDPI-aware cover thumbnails round out the tiling ergonomics.

Audit sweep: a 63-test unit suite, clean lint, and a round of bugfixes covering the hover-glow color bleed, search-parser clause dropping, Recently Read state handling, breakpoint precedence, cold-cache cover starvation, and author ordering.
Flatpak manifest targeting GNOME 50 — builds end-to-end with flatpak-builder; bundled hermitage-verify reads the host library through the sandbox.
Application icon — Fraunces-inspired serif H monogram on a deep aubergine card with warm candlelight glow.
Library export to JSON or CSV; toast notification system.
Library Insights window — at-a-glance counters, top tags/authors, format coverage, library hygiene audit.
Series browser sibling to the genre browser.
Identifier links in the Codex (Open Library, Goodreads, Google Books, Amazon, StoryGraph, Hardcover, FictionDB, DOI, …) plus tag-hierarchy search parity with cquarry.
Reading history — local SQLite event log, Codex "Last read" line, grid read indicator, "Recently Read" virtual library row.
Phase 7 complete: empty states, error resilience, and the database-lock snapshot fallback.
